21 New Watches You Missed from Timex, Blancpain, Grand Seiko and More

Keep time with watchmaking’s most exciting new releases.

By Johnny Brayson, Ethan Brehm, Brad Lanphear, Steve Mazzucchi, and Sean Tirman

Published August 23, 2026

·

If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:59
Instaread

From afar, the watch industry may seem unhurried. But every passing day brings about new timepieces from brands big, small, new and old. Below, find dozens of new releases from affordable watchmakers and luxury legends alike.

Together, they show an industry that never stops ticking — and, centuries later, can still find the time to surprise you.

Video Muted

Timex Expedition Pioneer Automatic

The Expedition Pioneer Automatic turns the existing Expedition Pioneer GMT into a time-and-date field watch with diver specs. It is available with a black dial and bezel on a stainless steel bracelet, and a blue dial and bezel on a brown leather strap. Both feature the same yellow seconds hand copied from the existing GMT hand, and run on a Miyota Caliber 8215 automatic movement.
  • $459 at Timex (Black)
  • $429 at Timex (Blue)

Peanuts x Timex Waterbury Classic 40mm

Timex originally released a Snoopy-leaping-into-leaves dial back in 2020, and it sold out fast. This Waterbury Classic revival makes a strong case for being the better version. The case steps up from low-lead brass to stainless steel, the bezel trades in its rounder profile for something cleaner and more wearable, and a Leather Working Group-certified black leather strap replaces the original’s brown. Snoopy now jumps solo from the right side on a white dial but it’s still a perfect autumnal watch for the upcoming season.
  • $189 at Timex

Timex Expedition Field Post Titanium Automatic Black

Timex adds a black IP coating to its shock-resistant titanium field watch, adding to a list of specs that include a sapphire crystal, Japanese automatic movement, Super-LumiNova and more.
  • $429 at Timex

Timex Q Timex Continental Chronograph 36mm

It’s only been a few months and Timex is already refining one of our favorite collections. The new 36mm Continental Chronograph dials back the case size from 40mm and swaps the color-matched tachymeter bezels for clean steel rings. Stepped bicompax registers replace the flatter originals, adding visual depth to the radial dial texture we already loved. Three colorways are available: light blue, panda and a two-tone champagne that nails the ’70s spirit the Continental line was built on.
  • $259 at Timex

Peanuts x Timex Expedition Acadia 40mm Silicone Strap Watch

Snoopy trades his doghouse for the trail on this Expedition Acadia, a field-ready 40mm quartz built around a lightweight matte-black resin case with a crown guard. Available in cream and green, the dials carry camouflage-themed Beagle Scouts artwork, luminant hands and markers for low-light legibility, and a date window for practical utility. A quick-release grooved silicone strap and 50m water resistance round out the package, making it a solid pick for outdoor enthusiasts who want a little Peanuts charm on the wrist.
  • $119 at Timex

Tissot PRX 40mm

Tissot adds a waffle-textured mother-of-pearl dial, previously only available on the smaller 35mm automatic PRX, to the larger 40mm Powermatic 80 in stainless steel.
  • $850 at Tissot

Nodus Sector II DIVE Holme & Hadfield Edition

Nodus teams up with a celebrated display case manufacturer to create a sapphire dial that appears to suspend the hour markers and brand logos above the dial plate. The fluted bezel frame and knurled crown are bronze, and the bezel insert is DLC steel. It features the standard 40mm stainless steel Sector Dive case and three-link stainless steel bracelet, offering 100m water resistance. It is a limited edition of 75 pieces, with an early access signup available for August 27 and a public sale on August 28.
  • $650 at Nodus Watches

Czapek Promenade Transparencies Aqua Blue

Czapek adds a smoked blue sapphire dial to its Promenade to properly show off the fully skeletonized in-house Calibre SXH7 automatic micro-rotor movement.
  • $40,300 at Czapek Genève

Blancpain Fifty Fathoms Bathyscaphe 70th Anniversary

Blancpain marks 70 years of the Bathyscaphe skin diver by recreating an iconic 1968 reference, right down to its compact 37mm case size.
  • $18,300 at Blancpain

Glashütte Original Senator Chronograph Navigator

The Senator Chronograph Navigator draws direct inspiration from 1940s pilot’s watches, including sword hands, large arabic numerals and a bicompax layout. A new, slightly shrunken 41mm stainless steel case houses the in-house Caliber 37-24 automatic, which delivers a flyback chronograph, Panorama Date and a 70-hour power reserve. It is available on a sand-colored nylon strap, a black leather strap and a steel bracelet.
  • $16,100 at Glashütte Original

Casio G-Shock Move GBA-950-1A4

The G-Shock GBA-950 Series pairs sporty styling with daily training capabilities and legendary Japanese formidability. It taps your phone’s GPS for precise distance calibration, then tracks pace, auto-laps, steps, and calories burned independently, and it is all compatible with Strava, the world-famous training app and social network. The origami-engineered band and bezel are seamlessly molded into one piece: a carbon fiber-reinforced resin case wrapped in a construction designed for all-day wrist comfort on and off the road (or trails).
  • $165 at Casio

Casio Edifice EFS-S660D-1A Solar Powered Chronograph

Casio debuts a new chronograph that does its best luxury sports watch impression. The Edifice EFS-S660D-1A packs motorsport-ready function into a slim, 38.3mm stainless-steel case, which is more compact than its past options. A solar-powered quartz movement keeps it self-sufficient, while a sapphire crystal with anti-reflective coating protects the honeycomb-textured dial. The tachymeter bezel and 1/20-second chronograph serve up genuine utility for speed enthusiasts, and 100m water resistance provides extra versatility for a decent price.
  • Learn More

Grand Seiko SBGA527

Limited to just 50 pieces and only available in Honolulu, this Grand Seiko Heritage Collection piece features a 40mm 62GS case and bracelet in High Intensity Titanium, Spring Drive movement and a blue textured dial inspired by the serene waters off Japan’s and Hawaii’s finest beaches.
  • $7,600 at Grand Seiko

Norqain Independence Skeleton Titanium DLC

Norqain updates its Independence Skeleton sports watch with a lightweight Grade 5 titanium case featuring a black DLC coating, making the watch considerably lighter than its steel predecessor.
  • $5,850 at Norqain

Minase Mastercraft J3

Inspired by one of Minase’s earliest designs, the Mastercraft J3 distills everything the Akita-based boutique manufacturer does well into a slim 37mm stainless-steel package. The Miyota Caliber 90S5 automatic movement foregoes the brand’s typical Swiss selections to keep this design affordable. The ultra-thin movement operates a three-hand, time-only dial with a sand-textured finish, available in silver, black and cream.
  • $2,050 at Minase Watches

Citizen Eco-Drive One AR5065-54W

At just 3.88mm thick, the Citizen Eco-Drive One AR5065-54W is a “marvel of micro-engineering,” to use the brand’s own words. Its 38mm black DLC-coated stainless steel case frames a two-tone dial with rose gold hands (and other details), alongside minimalist indices. Citizen’s Caliber 8826 solar movement pulls power from any light source, holding a charge for up to a year. However, it is limited to 250 pieces worldwide, making this a rarefied masterwork that’ll be hard to come by.
  • $3,395 at Citizen

Shinola Detrola Watch (Color Theory Cool)

Shinola’s Detrola Color Theory Cool turns the dial into a canvas: pink and blue triangles dance across the face in a pattern that nods to mid-century American art, with a mint green second hand and C1 lume-tipped gray hands finishing the picture. The 41mm case pairs a stainless steel core with co-molded cream TR90 resin for a watch that’s lighter than it looks, while a clear exhibition caseback lets you glimpse the Ronda Argonite 705 quartz movement at work. Like its orange-heavy Color Theory Warm counterpart, this watch is designed and assembled in Detroit.
  • $495 at Shinola

Boldr x Windup Watch Shop Venture Windup Edition 3

The third chapter of Boldr and Windup Watch Shop’s long-running Venture collaboration arrives with the most ambitious dial yet. It features lumicast block indices, oversized numerals at 15, 45 and 60, a crosshair motif and a date window at 6:00. The foundation remains a 38mm titanium case, AR-coated sapphire crystal, Seiko NH35 automatic and 200m of water resistance. Limited to 100 pieces, available exclusively from Windup Watch Shop.
  • $429 at Windup Watch Shop

Rado Captain Cook X European Cricket Special Edition

Rado celebrates its position as European Cricket’s official timekeeper with this special-edition Captain Cook diver featuring a two-tone gold PVD case and bracelet, blue dial and ceramic bezel insert, and two additional straps.
  • $3,000 at Rado

Kiwame Tokyo Yane

Japanese independent brand Kiwame Tokyo draws inspiration for its first rectangular watch from the temple rooftops of Asakusa. The Yane Kuro pairs a black lacquer dial with a 316L stainless-steel case whose swept profile mirrors a temple roof’s silhouette, while the Yane Enji presents the same design in burgundy. It is powered by a regulated Miyota Caliber 6T27 automatic with a 40-hour power reserve.
  • $730 at Kiwame Tokyo

Furlan Marri Outback Songlines

One of seven watches from seven independent brands created for Time & Tide’s first Founder’s Fest, the Outback Songlines is an evolution of Furlan Marri’s earlier T&T collab, the Outback Elegy. The watch introduces a new 39mm steel case complete with a fitted three-row steel braceleet, a first for the brand. The dial keeps its chocolate brown color, with a trio of finishes (grained, brushed and lacquered) ensure its appearance is constantly in flux. The most exciting detail, however, is the caseback. It’s a rare hinged officer-style caseback, and opening it reveals a window to the La Joux-Perret G100 automatic movement and its 68-hour power reserve. Like the other Founder’s Fest releases, the watch will only be available during a 24-hour window in September. Register your interest at the Founder’s Fest site to get notified when it’s time to buy.
  • $2,750 at Time & Tide
About the Author:

Johnny Brayson is an editor at Gear Patrol mostly covering watches. He enjoys watches that are packed with blink-and-you’ll-miss-’em details and believes nearly every watch could stand to be a tad smaller.
